record.paper_title: Electromagnetic probes in heavy-ion collisions: progress and open questions
record.original_question: For photon and dilepton emission from viscous hydrodynamic simulations of heavy-ion collisions, how can one determine the exact energy and momentum distribution of the additional electromagnetic radiation produced when the plasma is out of local thermal equilibrium, given that viscosity generates entropy and that the non-equilibrium emission rate must be related to microscopic quark, gluon, or hadron momentum distributions and to hydrodynamic quantities such as bulk pressure and shear stress?

evidence.quote: One challenge of the “macroscopic” approach is when the medium deviates from local equilibrium, as is the case in viscous hydrodynamics simulations of heavy-ion collisions.

One expects more photons and dileptons to be produced in this non-equilibrium case than in the local equilibrium case, as a result of the additional entropy generated. Determining the exact energy and momentum distribution of these additional photons and dileptons is not trivial.

the viscous energy-momentum tensor is related to a certain form for the momentum distribution of quarks and gluons, or of hadrons (“Grad”, “Chapman-Enskog”, “Romatschke-Strickland”, ...), and a non-equilibrium electromagnetic emission rate is computed
where the viscous part of the energy-momentum tensor was decomposed into the shear stress π^{μν} component and the bulk pressure Π component.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a relativistic plasma described by viscous hydrodynamics whose energy–momentum tensor admits a Landau-frame decomposition
T^{μν} = ε u^μ u^ν − (P + Π) Δ^{μν} + π^{μν},
where ε is the energy density, P the equilibrium pressure, u^μ the fluid four-velocity, Δ^{μν} = g^{μν} − u^μ u^ν the spatial projector, Π the bulk-viscous pressure, and π^{μν} the (traceless, transverse) shear-stress tensor. The microscopic degrees of freedom are quarks and gluons at high temperatures and hadrons at low temperatures, with single-particle phase-space distributions
f(x,p) = f_eq(x,p) + δf_shear(x,p; π^{μν}) + δf_bulk(x,p; Π),
where the non-equilibrium corrections δf are functionals of π^{μν} and Π whose form depends on the chosen ansatz (e.g. Grad's 14-moment, Chapman–Enskog, Romatschke–Strickland).

The differential emission rate of real photons and of dileptons from such a medium is, at leading order in the electromagnetic coupling, a convolution of the partonic/hadronic matrix elements with products of the distributions f and of Bose/Fermi factors (1 ± f).

Problem. Determine, from first principles in QCD (and from the relevant hadronic effective theories in the confined phase), the exact energy- and momentum-differential emission rates
dN_γ/(d^4x d^3k)   and   dN_{ℓ⁺ℓ⁻}/(d^4x d^4q)
of photons and dileptons emitted by the plasma when it is out of local thermal equilibrium, expressed as explicit functionals of the local hydrodynamic variables (T, u^μ, π^{μν}, Π) through the underlying microscopic distributions f_eq + δf_shear + δf_bulk, in such a way that:
(i) the result is independent of the (unphysical) choice of δf-ansatz to the order in gradients considered;
(ii) it reproduces the known equilibrium rate in the limit π^{μν}, Π → 0;
(iii) it consistently accounts for the additional electromagnetic radiation associated with the entropy produced by viscous dissipation.
artifact.status_search_result: Multiple recent works compute viscous corrections to photon and dilepton rates using specific δf ansätze (Grad, Chapman–Enskog, Romatschke–Strickland) and holographic or kinetic-theory approaches, but none provide a complete, ansatz-independent first-principles determination of the full non-equilibrium emission spectrum incorporating both shear and bulk corrections; the problem remains an active area of research with partial results only.

status_evidence.title: Viscous corrections to electromagnetic emissivities in QCD
status_evidence.snippet: Computes viscous corrections to photon emission rates; bulk corrections sizable, shear smaller.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for viscous corrections using specific kinetic-theory ansätze.

status_evidence.title: Bulk viscous effects on flow and dilepton radiation in a hybrid approach
status_evidence.snippet: Studies bulk viscous corrections to dilepton emission within hybrid hydrodynamic simulations.
status_evidence.claim: Bulk-viscous dilepton rates are computed model-dependently.

status_evidence.title: Out-of-equilibrium photon production in a holographic Bjorken expanding plasma
status_evidence.snippet: Holographic study of out-of-equilibrium photon emission, complementary to kinetic-theory approaches.
status_evidence.claim: Alternative approaches yield only partial, model-dependent answers.

status_evidence.title: A Non-Equilibrium Approach to Photon Emission from the Late Stages of Heavy-Ion Collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Non-equilibrium hadronic photon emission treated approximately.
